title: Cristiano Ronaldo Reportedly Set to End Portugal Career in September Nations League Match
excerpt: The 41-year-old is expected to make his final international appearance against Wales at Estadio Jose Alvalade — the same venue where his Portugal journey began in 2003.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Cristiano Ronaldo plans to retire from international football after the September 24 match against Wales.
  • He holds records for 146 international goals and 233 appearances for Portugal.
  • Ronaldo's career includes a European Championship win and two UEFA Nations League titles.
  • He continues his club career at Al-Nassr, nearing 1,000 career goals with 976 scored.

Cristiano Ronaldo is reportedly planning to end his record-breaking international career after one final Portugal appearance in a UEFA Nations League match against Wales on September 24, according to Goal.com.

https://x.com/FootballTalkHQ/status/2080332135492456698

The match at Sporting Lisbon's Estadio Jose Alvalade would bring Ronaldo's Portugal story full circle — it was at that same ground that a teenage Ronaldo made his senior international debut in August 2003, in a friendly against Kazakhstan.

A Career of Unprecedented Scale

Ronaldo's international numbers stand alone in football history. In 233 appearances, the forward has scored 146 goals and provided 45 assists, making him both the most-capped men's international footballer and the all-time leading scorer. He holds 87 more caps than Portugal's second-most-capped player, Joao Moutinho, and has 99 more goals than the country's number two scorer, Pauleta.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=G2aQCFf4wcw

"Enjoy it while it lasts. It's not today that he's saying goodbye, but it's soon. I believe this is his last dance."

— Katia Aveiro, Ronaldo's sister, speaking to SportTV

His trophy cabinet with Portugal includes the European Championship in 2016 — a landmark title won on French soil — and two UEFA Nations League triumphs in 2019 and 2025.

World Cup Exit and What Followed

The retirement reports come weeks after Portugal's elimination from the 2026 World Cup, where Spain knocked them out in the Round of 16. Ronaldo scored three goals in five matches at the tournament, including a brace against Uzbekistan in the group stage and a penalty against Croatia in the Round of 32. He played 441 minutes across the competition.

Ronaldo had already confirmed before the tournament that the 2026 edition would be his last World Cup. The question of whether he would continue with Portugal beyond it had lingered since, with his sister's comments to Portuguese outlet SportTV fueling speculation that retirement was imminent.

![Estadio Jose Alvalade. Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/42/Est%C3%A1dio_Jos%C3%A9_Alvalade_antes_do_jogo_Sporting_-_Arouca.jpg/3840px-Est%C3%A1dio_Jos%C3%A9_Alvalade_antes_do_jogo_Sporting_-_Arouca.jpg)

New Coach, Same Captain — For Now

Portugal recently appointed Jorge Jesus as head coach on a four-year deal. Jesus has signaled continuity rather than revolution. "People might think that the new manager is going to come in and change a lot of players. That won't happen. I'm not stupid," he told Canal 11.

The report, which originated from Goal.com's Moataz Elgammal citing a Portuguese football agent, has not been officially confirmed by either Ronaldo or the Portuguese Football Federation. Ronaldo himself addressed retirement talk during the World Cup in characteristically measured fashion.

"I don't make decisions on the spur of the moment anymore; now I take everything calmly. For now, it's about enjoying today."

— Cristiano Ronaldo

The Road to 1,000 Goals

Even if September marks his international farewell, Ronaldo's playing career is far from over. His contract with Saudi Pro League side Al-Nassr runs through June 2027, when he will be 42. He has scored 123 goals in 142 games across all competitions for the club.

Ronaldo's Journey to 1,000 Goals
›Currently has 976 career goals across club and country.
›Contract with Al-Nassr runs through June 2027.
›Scored 123 goals in 142 games for Al-Nassr.
›New manager known for attacking football may boost goal tally.

The five-time Ballon d'Or winner currently sits on 976 career goals across club and country, with the symbolic 1,000-goal milestone firmly in sight. With Al-Nassr's new manager Ange Postecoglou — a coach known for attacking football — and a squad featuring Kingsley Coman, Sadio Mane, and Joao Felix, Ronaldo's pursuit of four figures appears well within reach over the coming season.

If the September 24 match against Wales does prove to be Ronaldo's final bow, it will close a 23-year international career that reshaped the record books and redefined what longevity at the highest level looks like.
